explanation: Erdős #1194: for a perfect difference set A ⊆ ℕ (every n ≥ 1 is uniquely a_n − b_n), how fast must a_n/n increase? Perfect difference sets are encoded over ℤ via IsPerfectDifferenceSet A 0, excluding 0. a_n is correctly the larger element of the representation (unique by the API lemma). "Must increase" is formalized as the set of monotone G such that every such A has a_n ≥ c·G(n)·n infinitely often. That is a reasonable formalization; the site gives a_n ≫ n log n infinitely often, and a_n ≪ n³ for the greedy construction. The statement is faithful and open.
